item.title: Rodri ends Man City spell, joins Barca

item.content:encoded:
BARCELONE have signed midfielder Rodri from Manchester City on a deal until June 2030, the LaLiga champions announced on Tuesday, ending the Spaniard’s glittering, trophy-laden spell with the Premier League club in a major coup for the Catalan side.

The 30-year-old joins Hansi Flick’s side for a reported fee of 65.4 million pounds ($88.56 million), with Barca beating arch-rivals Real Madrid to the Spain international’s signature.

Rodri’s contract with City had been due to expire in June 2027.

“FC Barcelona and Manchester City have reached an agreement for the transfer of Rodrigo Hernandez Cascante, known in the football world as Rodri, who is committing to the Catalan club until 30 June 2030,” Barca said in a statement. The 2024 Ballon d’Or winner, who was also part of Spain’s European Championship winning squad, further enhanced his reputation by captaining his country to World Cup glory last month and was named the tournament’s best player.

Rodri leaves City after winning four Premier League titles, the Champions League and two FA Cups since joining the English club from Atletico Madrid in 2019. He made 298 appearances, scoring 28 goals and helping City secure 14 major trophies.

He spent six seasons under Pep Guardiola, establishing himself as one of the world’s best midfielders and playing a pivotal role in City’s continental treble in the 2022-23 season. He also helped City become the first men’s top-flight club in English football history to win four consecutive Premier League titles.

But the last two years have also been marked by injury setbacks. He spent more than seven months on the sidelines after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury in 2024, while he also dealt with knee and hamstring problems last season. Rodri arrives at Camp Nou after recently undergoing minor back surgery, a setback that was expected to keep him out for the start of the season.

item.title: All Blacks hope duo will be fit
item.description: NEW Zealand should be able to use record try scorer Will Jordan and scrumhalf Cam Roigard in Saturday’s first Test against the Springboks despite the pair having yet to feature on the tour of South Africa. Coach Dave Rennie said he expected both players to be ready to play in the first of the four Tests at Ellis Park and was not concerned they had not had pre-test practice.
item.content:encoded:
NEW Zealand should be able to use record try scorer Will Jordan and scrumhalf Cam Roigard in Saturday’s first Test against the Springboks despite the pair having yet to feature on the tour of South Africa.

Coach Dave Rennie said he expected both players to be ready to play in the first of the four Tests at Ellis Park and was not concerned they had not had pre-test practice.

“Cam has played a lot of rugby this year, so him not playing so much lately is not a bad thing,” Rennie told a press conference on Monday.

“Will came into that French test on the back of being out for a long time, so we’re confident they will slot straight in.

“They are clear on our structures and their roles within the team, so we’re just making sure they are physically ready to go.”

item.title: Back to basics
item.description: VODAFONE Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker says the team’s immediate focus is on building a strong foundation as they prepare for their upcoming Test against Japan. Walker believes the work done so far is only the beginning of a long-term plan aimed at developing players’ conditioning, skills and decision-making.
item.content:encoded:
VODAFONE Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker says the team’s immediate focus is on building a strong foundation as they prepare for their upcoming Test against Japan.

Walker believes the work done so far is only the beginning of a long-term plan aimed at developing players’ conditioning, skills and decision-making.

“It’s just a continuation of what we started. We went back to basics, we stripped it all back to the fundamentals of rugby. We’ve just got to continue over the next two to three weeks to build on those aspects of the game,” Walker said.

The Fijiana would use the coming weeks, Walker said, to strengthen key areas rather than trying to introduce complicated systems that are beyond the team’s current capabilities.

“Our focus as we move towards Japan will just be to tidy up small aspects of our game. Again, we’re not trying to do things that are outside of our reach.

“We want to stay within what we can do and what we’re capable of. We just have to be more accurate around some of the decision-making and then the skill-set stuff.”

The coach stressed that accuracy would be one of the biggest areas of focus as the team continues its preparations.

“That’ll be one of the key focuses over the next few weeks, making sure that we stay accurate with what we’re trying to do, but we’re continuing to learn new things and we’re challenging ourselves at the same time.”

Walker, who is still getting to know the players and their individual strengths, said the program also provides an opportunity to identify and develop talent capable of progressing to the next level.

“Another exciting thing for me is that I come in with fresh eyes and an opportunity to try and see who these players are, where they’re from and hopefully continue to give players opportunities to thrive at that next level.”

With Japan ahead, Walker said the Fijiana’s preparation would remain firmly focused on gradual improvement, with conditioning, skill development and decision-making forming the foundation of their long-term progress.

item.title: Origin Game II to be played at Eden Park
item.description: AUSTRALIAN rugby league’s showpiece event will head across the Tasman for the first time, with the men’s State of Origin confirmed for Auckland next year. The Australian Rugby League Commission (ARLC) announced on Tuesday that Game II of the 2027 series will be played at Auckland’s Eden Park. item.content:encoded:
AUSTRALIAN rugby league’s showpiece event will head across the Tasman for the first time, with the men’s State of Origin confirmed for Auckland next year.

The Australian Rugby League Commission (ARLC) announced on Tuesday that Game II of the 2027 series will be played at Auckland’s Eden Park. It will be only the second time State of Origin has been played outside Australia, with California hosting a match in 1987 at Veterans Memorial Stadium, which was won by the Blues 30-18. ARLC chairman Peter V’landys said the Origin match, scheduled for June 16, 2027, would be part of a wider rugby league festival in New Zealand’s largest city.

“State of Origin is truly unique. It creates an atmosphere unlike anything else in Australian sport — fierce rivalry, raw passion and an intensity that can only be understood by experiencing it firsthand. It’s a bucket-list event,” V’landys said.

“It’s not just the Origin match fans can look forward to – we are planning a week of rugby league festivities in the lead-up to the event, starting with a Warriors game at Eden Park on the Sunday afternoon prior to the Origin fixture. It’s going to be a complete takeover of Auckland, showcasing the best of our game to New Zealanders and fans travelling from all over the world.”

Despite being a contest between Queensland and New South Wales, the State of Origin series has garnered widespread interest since its inception in 1980. Eligibility rules were changed this year to allow some players to represent Queensland or New South Wales, but then be selected for New Zealand and England in the Test area.

Kalyn Ponga, Addin Fonua-Blake and Briton Nikora all played in this year’s Origin series and will be available for Kiwi selection at this year’s World Cup.

item.title: No clear favourite
item.description: THE Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship remains wide open after an action-packed opening day in Labasa yesterday produced no clear favourite. Fiji Secondary Schools Football Association president Aminesh Ram said several established teams boasting district representatives had struggled, while lesser-known players and schools had risen to the occasion.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship remains wide open after an action-packed opening day in Labasa yesterday produced no clear favourite.

Fiji Secondary Schools Football Association president Aminesh Ram said several established teams boasting district representatives had struggled, while lesser-known players and schools had risen to the occasion.

“The competition has been quite tough,” Ram said. “The renowned teams with district representatives have failed to shine, while teams with relatively unknown players have stepped up and managed to beat some of the bigger schools and teams.”

In the under-19 grade, Labasa College opened its campaign with a 2-0 win over Tilak High School, while Labasa Muslim College edged Labasa Sangam College 2-1.

Vunimono High School and Gurunanak Khalsa College played to a scoreless draw, while Rishikul Sanatan College lost 1-0 to Labasa College. Labasa Sangam College defeated Nadroga Arya College 2-0.

At the Fiji Football Academy, Xavier College and Nadi Sangam College drew 0-0, while Suva Muslim College lost 1-0 to Ba Sangam College. All Saints Secondary School and Vunimono High School also played to a scoreless draw.

At the Labasa College ground, Tavua College defeated All Saints 1-0, while Central College edged Bucalevu 1-0.

Central College also recorded a 2-0 win over Tavua College in the under-15 grade, while DAV College lost 1-0 to Ba Sangam in the under-17 grade.

At the Labasa Sangam College venue, Vashist Muni College defeated Lautoka Muslim College 2-0, while Swami Vivekananda College went down 1-0 to Penang Sangam College.

Central College defeated Labasa Muslim College 1-0 in the under-17 grade.

With the final round of pool matches scheduled to be played across six venues in Labasa today, Ram said teams could not afford to relax.

“It will now come down to strategy. Everybody has played at least one game, and how they approach the final day will matter a lot,” he said.

Ram said the tournament had already produced a high standard of football, with several players attracting the selectors’ attention.

“The competition level has been very high, with a lot of talent on display. Tomorrow is another big day of football that we can expect from all the teams,” he said.

With quarter-final places at stake, Ram said no team could consider itself safe.

The championship has brought together 41 teams from Viti Levu and Vanua Levu.

Ram said the performances of smaller schools had added another dimension to the competition and urged supporters to turn out in numbers for another exciting day of secondary schools football.

item.title: Weight of hopes
item.description: THE weight of Marist Brothers High School’s hopes now rests on a group of teenagers who have earned the right to dream big. The school’s under-15 side will be its lone representative in the Vodafone Super Deans finals after last Saturday’s gritty 16-3 victory over Lelean Memorial School at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva.
item.content:encoded:
THE weight of Marist Brothers High School’s hopes now rests on a group of teenagers who have earned the right to dream big.

The school’s under-15 side will be its lone representative in the Vodafone Super Deans finals after last Saturday’s gritty 16-3 victory over Lelean Memorial School at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva.

For the U15 players, the final is more than another match. It is an opportunity to finish what they started last year.

The side reached the national semi-finals last season but fell short of the decider. Twelve months on, they had gone one step further and now stand on the brink of a chance at national glory.

Captain Augustine Paul said the achievement had given the players plenty to be proud of.

“We feel really proud. We’re really happy,” Paul said.

“The boys, my brothers, they’re really happy to reach the final this year, as we reached the national semi-finals last year.”

Their semi-final victory was built on resilience.

Marist spent long periods inside their own red zone, but held their composure to restrict Lelean to just three points and secured their place in the final.

Paul knows there is still work to do, particularly with their exit play, before they face Ratu Kadavulevu School in the final.

“The message from the head coach was to improve on our exit play, as we were playing in our red zone for half of the game,” he said.

“We’ll try to iron out our mistakes this week and come back stronger.”

Paul expects RKS to provide another stern test.

The skipper dedicated the semi-final victory to their parents, the Marist family and God.

“We’d like to dedicate this win to the parents, to the Marist family, and to the Lord Almighty.”

Now the U15 side carries the hopes of the entire Marist school into the final.

They are no longer simply last year’s semi-finalists.

They are finalists — and one victory away from turning unfinished business into championship glory.

“There’s still a lot to improve on,” Paul said.

item.title: Schools to drive new era of Fiji rugby league
item.description: SCHOOLS will form the backbone of a new rugby league development program in Fiji, with Australian Rugby League Commission (ARLC) commissioner Peter Beattie revealing plans to introduce the sport to children from as young as five. Beattie made the comments during an ARLC visit to Rishikul Nadera Primary School on Monday, as part of the newly established 10-year partnership with the Fiji National Ru
item.content:encoded:
SCHOOLS will form the backbone of a new rugby league development program in Fiji, with Australian Rugby League Commission (ARLC) commissioner Peter Beattie revealing plans to introduce the sport to children from as young as five.

Beattie made the comments during an ARLC visit to Rishikul Nadera Primary School on Monday, as part of the newly established 10-year partnership with the Fiji National Rugby League.

He said the ARLC would work with the Education Department to develop a program that could be introduced in schools and provide children with opportunities to participate and develop through rugby league.

“We’ll be working with the Education Department, who we met yesterday (Monday), to come up with a program to be implemented in schools, obviously from an early age, even from five years old, all the way through, so that young people reach their full potential,” Beattie said.

The program will include a non-contact component, with a strong focus on encouraging both boys and girls to participate.

Beattie said the aim was not simply to identify future NRL players, but to use sport as a way of helping young Fijians lead healthier and more active lives.

“Some will have pathways where they go to become NRL players, both boys and girls, and some will never go to that level, which is fine,” he said.

“We just want young Fijians, as part of this program, to live a long, healthy life.”

Beattie said school competitions would also be developed, although the details would be worked out in consultation with the Education Department.

He stressed that rugby league would not be positioned as a rival to rugby union, saying young Fijians should be able to participate in both codes.

“We’re not in competition with the rugby union, they will have competitions, we will have competitions, players will play both rugby union and rugby league, and that’s fine,” he said.

item.title: Local prop earns chance
item.description: FOR years, Inoke Ravuiwasa has worked his way through Fiji’s domestic rugby ranks with one goal in mind — earning an opportunity at the highest level. The experienced tighthead prop has been signed by the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua for the 2027 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season, rewarding a career built on perseverance, discipline and sacrifice.
item.content:encoded:
FOR years, Inoke Ravuiwasa has worked his way through Fiji’s domestic rugby ranks with one goal in mind — earning an opportunity at the highest level.

The experienced tighthead prop has been signed by the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua for the 2027 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season, rewarding a career built on perseverance, discipline and sacrifice.

Originally from Tavuki, Taveuni, with maternal links to Susui, Vanuabalavu in Lau, Ravuiwasa has been a consistent performer in Fiji’s provincial competitions and a long-serving member of the Fiji Police rugby team.

He most recently represented Suva in the Skipper Cup after spending part of the 2026 season in Australia with the Western Districts Lions in Canberra’s John I Dent Cup.

His pathway to the Drua has also included representative rugby, having been part of the Fiji under-20 setup in 2016 alongside current Drua co-captains Temo Mayanavanua and Frank Lomani.

He later represented the Fijian Warriors against Australia Country in October last year and was also part of the Skipper Select side that faced the Drua in the club’s 2026 pre-season trial.

For Ravuiwasa, the signing is the reward for years of persistence.

“I’ve been working towards making this team for a long time, so to finally get this opportunity means a lot to me,” he said.

“All the sacrifices, perseverance and discipline over the years have paid off.”

The 30-year-old said the opportunity would only strengthen his determination to prove himself at Super Rugby Pacific level.

“I’m very grateful to the Drua management for giving me this opportunity, and I’ll continue to work hard, especially heading into the new season.”

Drua general manager Rugby Baden Stephenson said Ravuiwasa’s persistence had earned him his chance.

“He is an experienced and powerful tighthead prop who has consistently performed in Fiji’s domestic competitions, and his hard work and persistence over the years have earned him this opportunity,” Stephenson said.
